title: The ATF5-GPER1 axis drives female protection in hepatocellular carcinoma through dual tumor-suppressive and immune-modulatory mechanisms.
authors: Xu, Zhiquan; Wang, Hao; He, Qiang; Cui, Hongshuai; Wu, Zhongjun; Liao, Rui
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组和单细胞测序结合机器学习研究ATF5-GPER1轴在肝癌性别差异中的肿瘤抑制与免疫调节作用，虽涉及转录因子ATF5，但核心是表达与功能机制，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits marked sexual dimorphism, with females demonstrating superior survival, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomics (GSE39791, TCGA-LIHC, GSE14520) and single-cell RNA sequencing (five datasets, n = 58 patients, 238,982 cells) with machine learning (LASSO, SVM, random forest) to identify female-protective genes driving HCC disparities. Activating transcription factor 5 (ATF5) emerged as a female-protective gene with higher expression in females versus males across cohorts. Single-cell analyses revealed ATF5 defines a female-enriched, low-grade malignant subcluster with elevated apoptotic programs and reduced proliferative signaling, and pseudotime analysis showed coordinated ATF5-GPER1 downregulation during malignant progression (Spearman rho = -0.52 and -0.48; both p < 0.001). In the immune compartment, ATF5 marked a female-enriched IFN-gamma(+) macrophage state with enhanced immunostimulatory programs and preferential CXCL9/10-CXCR3-mediated communication with CD8/NK cells. Mechanistically, ATF5 transcriptionally activates G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1), forming an estrogen-responsive regulatory module that functionally suppresses proliferation, induces apoptosis (HepG2: 26.45% vs. 11.88%, p < 0.0001), and inhibits migration in a GPER1-dependent manner as demonstrated by rescue experiments. Tissue microarray validation (n = 167) confirmed high ATF5 expression predicts improved recurrence-free survival specifically in female patients (HR = 0.34, p = 0.040) but not males (p = 0.080). The ATF5-GPER1 axis represents a female-protective circuit operating through tumor-intrinsic suppression and immune remodeling, offering mechanistic insight into HCC sexual dimorphism and identifying ATF5 as a sex-specific prognostic biomarker with potential therapeutic implications.
abstract_zh: 肝细胞癌（HCC）表现出显著的性别二态性，女性患者的生存率更优，但其潜在分子机制尚不清楚。我们整合了批量转录组学（GSE39791、TCGA-LIHC、GSE14520）和单细胞RNA测序（五个数据集，n = 58例患者，238,982个细胞）以及机器学习（LASSO、SVM、随机森林），以识别驱动HCC差异的女性保护基因。激活转录因子5（ATF5）被鉴定为女性保护基因，在各队列中女性表达高于男性。单细胞分析显示，ATF5定义了一个女性富集的低级别恶性亚群，该亚群具有升高的凋亡程序和降低的增殖信号，拟时间分析显示在恶性进展过程中ATF5-GPER1协同下调（Spearman rho = -0.52和-0.48；均p < 0.001）。在免疫区室中，ATF5标记了一个女性富集的IFN-gamma(+)巨噬细胞状态，具有增强的免疫刺激程序，并优先通过CXCL9/10-CXCR3介导与CD8/NK细胞的通讯。机制上，ATF5转录激活G蛋白偶联雌激素受体1（GPER1），形成一个雌激素响应调控模块，该模块功能上抑制增殖、诱导凋亡（HepG2：26.45%对11.88%，p < 0.0001），并通过救援实验证明以GPER1依赖性方式抑制迁移。组织微阵列验证（n = 167）证实，高ATF5表达仅在女性患者中预测改善的无复发生存（HR = 0.34，p = 0.040），而在男性中不显著（p = 0.080）。ATF5-GPER1轴代表了一个通过肿瘤内在抑制和免疫重塑发挥作用的女性保护回路，为HCC性别二态性提供了机制见解，并将ATF5鉴定为具有潜在治疗意义的性别特异性预后生物标志物。
